status.comment: owner rulings 2026-08-26; harness-scoped campaign operations, not product semantics

p.STATUS-LINE: **Status: owner-ruled operating contract for the central OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex coordinator while the lifecycle/extensions campaign is active.** It consolidates worker routing, launcher use and test-panel cadence. It does not change VibeVM product semantics, Claude Code behavior, or a delegated packet.

scope.title: 1. Applicability — a harness gate, not a repository-wide mode

facts.OPENAI-CENTRAL-ONLY: This document applies only when the current owner-facing **central coordinator** runs under an OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex harness and is executing `campaigns/packages-2026-09/TZ-LIFECYCLE-EXTENSIONS-v0.1.md` (or the owner explicitly reactivates this contract by name). All conditions are required.
facts.NON-OPENAI-MUST-SKIP: Claude Code, a `claudez` process, Gemini and every other non-OpenAI harness MUST NOT read or apply this document. It is deliberately absent from the shared `STATIC.xml` / `INDEX.md` boot lane. The byte-identical `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`GEMINI.md` triplet carries one conditional pointer: an applicable OpenAI coordinator follows it; every other harness skips it.
facts.SUBAGENTS-MUST-SKIP: A task carrying `##subagent-quiet-clause`, a worker packet or an explicit reviewer packet is a subagent even when its executable is Codex. It follows that packet and MUST NOT promote itself to this central contract. Native workers, `codexrunner`, `claudez` and plain `claude` workers are all excluded by this rule.
facts.END-OF-CAMPAIGN: When the lifecycle campaign completes, pauses, or the owner selects another campaign, this contract becomes inactive without changing global project practice. A successor campaign needs an explicit owner ruling before it inherits any item.

facts.CENTRAL-OWNS-JUDGMENT: The central ChatGPT/Codex session owns architecture, cross-wave planning, owner rulings, destructive-action decisions, review verdicts, integration, staging allow-lists, commits, mirrors and final gates. A worker may propose or implement; it never self-accepts, moves authoritative status, commits, pushes or declares the campaign complete.
facts.DELEGATE-WHEN-CHEAPER-TO-VERIFY: Delegate a bounded task when independent verification is cheaper than generating it centrally. Keep a cross-cutting edit in one thread when its write perimeter intersects live atoms or correctness depends on an unresolved architectural choice.
facts.MODEL-DIVERSITY-IS-A-GATE: For a substantive implementation, prefer review by a different model family or fresh independent thread. Diversity counts only with exact file/line evidence, a root rerun of the decisive test and a mutation or negative oracle; another model's confidence is not evidence.
facts.CLAUDEZ-EXECUTES-ROOT-ACCEPTS: The owner assigns `claudez` execution priority, never acceptance authority. The central coordinator authors the architecture and packet, closes the write perimeter, names acceptance and red proofs, then reviews the result as a PR, reruns decisive tests/mutations and issues accept, same-cwd repair, re-commission or discard. Worker-written PASS/review/commit claims have zero authority; staging, commits, integration and final gates remain central.

p.POOL-IS-DYNAMIC: The pool is a set of interchangeable execution lanes with separate limits. Availability is probed on live work; no lane is assumed healthy from an old ping.

facts.NATIVE-WORKERS: **Native collaboration workers** are the low-latency fallback for a narrow edit/review that specifically benefits from current conversation context. They are not the default execution lane while `claudez` is healthy. Use disjoint write perimeters in parallel; retain packet/report/no-commit discipline.
facts.SOL-XHIGH: **`codexrunner` — `gpt-5.6-sol`, effort `xhigh`** — is the second external lane for hard, well-specified coding, broad code reading and mutation-backed repair when `claudez` is busy/limited or model diversity is useful. It runs in a dedicated worktree. Its yolo transport makes root diff review and a closed write allow-list mandatory; worker claims about review, commits or panels have no authority.
facts.CLAUDEZ-LANE: **`claudez`** is a strong implementation and review lane with an independent quota pool and is the **default first choice** for every new delegable packet while its live probe is healthy (owner priority ruling 2026-08-26). Its gateway may hit a five-hour account limit: probe with a real bounded task before fan-out, preserve the worktree/report/log and fail over to Sol/native instead of repeatedly paying a known 429 wall. `claudez2` remains disabled until the owner explicitly re-enables it.
facts.OPUS-MAX-LANE: **Plain Claude Code with Opus and max effort** is invoked explicitly as `claude --model opus --effort max`; follow-up repair uses `claude -c` in the exact same dedicated cwd. Use it for ambiguous code, adversarial architecture/code review, or difficult correction. Read run metadata to learn the resolved model; the alias is not proof of a version.
facts.NEVER-FABLE: **Never select Fable.** Do not name it, configure it as fallback, or accept automatic fallback to it. If Opus is unavailable, route to Sol, `claudez`, a native worker or the central coordinator.

facts.ROUTE-CODE: Hard but explicit code with a cheap oracle: `claudez` first; Sol xhigh next when the primary lane is unavailable or a second family is worth the spend. Use both concurrently only for disjoint writes. Ambiguous high-impact code: `claudez` may implement, but central/Opus/Sol independently reviews the judgment.
facts.ROUTE-REVIEW: Security, wire, transaction and lifecycle reviews: a fresh model family that did not author the change. Read-only reviews may run beside one code worker.
facts.ROUTE-MECHANICAL: Mechanical edits, fixtures, corpus additions and exact test matrices: `claudez` first, Sol/native on primary-lane limit or a genuine context advantage. The packet supplies the skeleton; the worker fills named refinement points rather than redrawing the architecture.
facts.ROUTE-MICRO-LOCAL: A deterministic micro-edit remains central when its complete implementation and oracle are cheaper than provisioning, reporting and reviewing an external worker. Measured 2026-08-26: one prescribed `specmark::scope!` line took `claudez` about 150 seconds plus packet/report review. Such a run is useful as an intentional transport/template probe, not the routine execution path. This is the verification-cheaper-than-generation law, not an exception to `claudez` priority for genuinely delegable work.
facts.ROUTE-CENTRAL: Architecture, provider boundaries, public grammar, final trade-offs, commit grouping and integration stay central. External architecture work is adversarial review of a central draft, not delegation of the final decision.

facts.ONE-CWD-ONE-THREAD: Every writing worker gets a dedicated worktree/cwd and packet file. Continuation (`-c`) is used only from that exact cwd. Large context travels in the packet file, never a command-line argument.
facts.CLAUDEZ-PERMISSION-RESET: Every `claudez -c` worker invocation explicitly sets `--permission-mode dontAsk` plus the positive `--allowedTools` list. A resumed Claude thread can otherwise retain `bypassPermissions` from its original session and execute a text-forbidden command despite a later allow-list. This was observed live when an R8 repair continuation ran a read-only `git diff` forbidden by its packet. The diff caused no mutation, but it proves the transport fence is not assumed. A later `dontAsk` run also executed benign `ls`/`grep` Bash not named by `--allowedTools`: that flag is an auto-approval list, **not** a closed capability universe. Pair it with explicit `--disallowedTools` patterns for forbidden command families; deny every ungranted built-in tool too. An isolated R8 specmap packet allowed only Read/Edit/Write textually and positively, yet the worker still invoked one Glob and two Grep calls because neither tool was explicitly disallowed. The worker disclosed the deviation and caused no out-of-perimeter mutation; textual bans and root artifact review remain mandatory.
facts.DISJOINT-WRITES: Parallelism is routed on write intersections, not read intersections. Read-only reviewers may overlap. Intersecting or many-place writes are serialized under one worker or the central coordinator.
facts.TWO-COLD-CARGO: The box ceiling is two simultaneous cold Cargo workers. Prefer one cargo-heavy implementation plus one cargo-heavy review/test at most; text/read-only workers may use otherwise free lanes. Cargo runs use `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` where the repository rule requires it.
facts.QUIET-ARTIFACT-CONTRACT: Every packet carries `##subagent-quiet-clause`, a closed write perimeter, exact acceptance, narrow self-verify commands, a durable `WORKER-REPORT-<id>.md`, a git/commit/push/full-panel ban and final `TASK-DONE`. Screen prose is discarded; reports and diffs are the deliverable.
facts.REPORT-BUDGET: Default a worker report to at most 150 lines: verdict, findings, changed-file set, decisive evidence, commands and deviations. A longer report is justified only by a large finding matrix or protocol review. Do not ask the worker to restate every source it read; exact citations replace narrative. The 2026-08-26 probes showed that a good Opus review can consume 47k output tokens and a GLM review 30k when no report budget is stated.
facts.NO-SECRETS-TO-WORKERS: Workers never receive token contents or a task that reads a token file. Secret-bearing live smoke stays central and prints only a safe verdict. Launchers load their own credentials without exposing them in packet, argv, log or report.
facts.LIMIT-FAILOVER: A quota/429/limit failure is transport state, not a code verdict. Confirm it once, keep partial artifacts, then re-route a fresh packet with durable context. Do not spin retries, kill by broad process name, or discard a useful diff because the runner exited non-zero.
facts.ROOT-ACCEPTANCE: Root acceptance compares actual changed files with the report, reads the diff as a PR, re-runs the decisive narrow command, executes the red mutation/negative oracle, and issues PASS, repair, re-commission or discard. Cosmetic tails are fixed centrally; wrong judgment or behavior uses same-cwd continuation when economical.

gates.title: 5. Fast development gates and the full-panel cadence

p.OWNER-PANEL-RULING: **Owner ruling, 2026-08-26:** the approximately twenty-minute full repository panel must not run after every small atom. During this ChatGPT campaign, exact tests are the development gate; the full panel is an integration/batch gate. This is the scoped successor to older campaign-TZ wording and changes no other project or harness.

facts.EXACT-GATES-PER-ATOM: Before accepting an atom, run formatting for each touched workspace, `git diff --check`, exact unit/integration tests for changed behavior, checks/clippy for touched crates, and the task-specific oracle: codegen idempotence plus wire corpus for schemas; byte identity for compiler changes; isolated homes for user-state code; a red mutation or independent negative fixture for every load-bearing branch. Expand only when dependency analysis names a real affected consumer.
facts.NO-WORKER-FULL-PANEL: A worker never runs the full panel. It runs the narrow self-verify named by its packet. The central coordinator does not run the full panel merely because a worker finished.
facts.ATOMIC-LOCAL-COMMITS: A coherent batch may contain several atomic local Conventional Commits, each accepted by its exact gate. They remain unmirrored until the batch integration panel is green. If that panel finds a defect, repair forward in the same batch and rerun newly relevant narrow tests before the next panel.
facts.FULL-PANEL-TRIGGERS: Run the full `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 tools/self-check.sh` panel when: **(1)** a cross-crate integration batch is ready to leave local state; **(2)** a lifecycle wave or owner scenario is declared green; **(3)** before mirror/push of accumulated code; **(4)** before final epic acceptance; **(5)** a high-risk change has no cheaper complete affected set. One panel may satisfy several triggers for the same unchanged tree.
facts.PANEL-IS-FOR-EXACT-TREE: A panel result belongs to the exact tree measured. A later product change invalidates it. A report/docs-only change runs its document gates and may ride the next integration panel, but cannot rewrite an earlier code verdict.
facts.MIRROR-AFTER-GREEN-BATCH: Mirror only after the accumulated batch panel is green and the staging allow-list is reviewed. This preserves atomic human-authored commits while amortising the slow panel over useful integration work.

facts.OBSERVE-NOT-ASSUME: Record only a live task's exit, durable report, resolved-model metadata and reviewed quality. A ping proves transport, not coding quality; an old successful run does not prove a five-hour quota remains open.
facts.PROBE-2026-08-26: Live work, not a ping, measured both extra lanes. `claudez` resolved to `glm-5.3[1m]`, completed an independent R7.1 review, found the missing blocking-HTTP timeouts, then used same-cwd `-c` to implement and gate the repair; root additionally repeated the Windows proxy canary 20 times. Plain Claude resolved to `claude-opus-5`, produced an adversarial build/package/deploy review and used same-cwd `-c` for nine central objections; it explicitly withdrew or narrowed four earlier claims and strengthened crash/ownership design. Both are high-quality usable lanes. Opus/max is reserved for ambiguous, high-impact judgment because the two passes were materially more costly; `claudez` is a parallel peer for bounded code/review but may hit its separate five-hour wall. Both exceeded the desired prose budget, so `##REPORT-BUDGET` is mandatory on future packets. After a later multi-hour network outage killed every live worker process, their worktrees and reports remained intact; a fresh isolated `claudez -p` returned exact `CLAUDEZ_OK` through `glm-5.3[1m]` in about nine seconds. Recovery is therefore census-first: retain completed artifacts and restart only unfinished packets, never regenerate the batch wholesale.
facts.CLAUDEZ-TURN-BUDGET: A 140-turn R8 continuation reached turn 141 and transport-failed **before writing its report**, despite useful code and focused-test progress; it emitted about 95k output tokens and repeatedly reran broad filters. Large continuation budgets invite scope accretion rather than completion. Default to a 30–50-turn bounded edit packet, split implementation from child-process tests/review, let root compile between packets, and reserve the final two worker turns for the durable report. `max_turns` exhaustion preserves the worktree but is never PASS.

claudez-template.title: 7. Canonical claudez packet template

p.TEMPLATE-IS-COPIED: The central coordinator copies this skeleton into every new `claudez` packet and fills every bracketed field. Do not point a worker at PROP-055 itself: this spec is ChatGPT-only. Task-specific instructions override a template default only when the packet says so explicitly.

claudez-template.fence:
# PACKET-<task-id> — <one bounded outcome>
## Role and authority
You are an EXECUTION worker, not the architect, reviewer, integrator or owner. The central coordinator owns architecture, acceptance, staging, commits and final gates. Your `PASS` is advisory. Do not claim that root reviewed/accepted anything. A prior report is a lead, never authority.
On a `-c` continuation, discard your previous verdict where the correction packet contradicts it. Re-read the correction packet first and repair the named failure; do not defend the old answer.
## Task
<exact behavior to implement or question to review>
## Required inputs
- <files/spec anchors/reports to read> - <facts supplied by root; confirm or refute each with exact evidence>
If an ambiguity would change public grammar, architecture, security posture or scope, STOP and write the exact blocker. Do not silently choose a new design.
## Write perimeter
- <closed list of files/directories allowed to change> - `WORKER-REPORT-<task-id>.md`
Every other path is read-only. Preserve pre-existing/user changes. Do not create a branch/worktree; root already provisioned the cwd. Do not spawn subagents.
## Acceptance
1. <criterion with observable result> 2. <negative/security/failure criterion> 3. <compatibility/idempotence criterion>
For every load-bearing branch name a RED proof: mutation or counterexample that fails when the guard is removed. An empty grep/test output is not proof until a known positive control demonstrates the instrument can fire.
## Constraints
- NO git command at all, including read-only `git diff/status/log`. - NO commit, push, merge, checkout, stash, reset, worktree or history action. - NO full repository panel; run only the exact commands listed below. - NO specs/status/SPEC-DEBT/WAL/CONTINUE/TASKS/BACKLOG/AGENTS/campaign edits. - NO network, publish, user-home mutation, token-file read or secret in argv/env/log/report unless this packet explicitly grants one exact operation. - NO shell file-writing tricks; use Edit/Write. Use `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`. - NO new `unsafe`, FFI, handwritten OS ABI or home-grown security/locking primitive unless the packet explicitly grants that architecture. Stop and report the missing primitive instead; do not invent a mini-runtime. - NO process/IDE manipulation. If a named verifier is blocked by an external file lock, report it; do not inspect or kill unrelated processes, rename a live generated tree, or hand-edit generated output as a substitute. - Every changed/new file remains at or below 600 physical lines. Check while editing; split early, not after fmt. - Do not weaken, delete or rewrite an oracle merely to make it green. - Treat a non-zero runner exit as transport state; still write durable evidence when possible.
## Allowed self-verify
```text <exact fmt/test/check/clippy/codegen commands; no broader substitutes> ```
## Deliverable report — draft within 140 lines
Do not spend turns repeatedly trimming a long report. Start concise (140-line target leaves headroom under a 150-line hard cap). Write/update the durable report before the final two allowed turns; a worker that reaches `max_turns` without it has failed its deliverable even when useful edits remain.
```markdown # WORKER-REPORT — <task-id> ## Verdict PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED (advisory only) ## Changed files - exact path — why ## Acceptance evidence - criterion → result, exact file:line/test output ## Red proofs - guard → mutation/counterexample ## Commands - command → exit + decisive lines ## Decisions and why - every choice within granted latitude, or none ## Deviations / forbidden-command incidents - disclose every deviation, including accidental git/network/broad test, or none ## Leftovers - exact remaining work, or none ```
## subagent-quiet-clause
Your screen text is discarded. Output only mandated `PROGRESS:` heartbeats, the durable report, and final `TASK-DONE`. No greeting, task restatement, intermediate chat reasoning or final screen summary.

facts.TEMPLATE-LAUNCH-GUARD: Launch with an explicit `--permission-mode dontAsk` and the smallest positive `--allowedTools` auto-approval set **plus explicit `--disallowedTools`** rules for git, process control and every task-specific forbidden shell family. For an edit packet this includes shell writers and interpreters (`python`, `perl`, `ruby`, `node`, `sed`, `awk`, `tee`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, PowerShell/cmd), not only git: R8 correction 3 used a Python heredoc to rewrite source despite the packet's Edit/Write-only clause. `allowedTools` alone does not deny an unlisted tool. Explicitly disallow every unused Claude tool class too (`Glob`, `Grep`, web, agents/tasks and notebook tools when not granted); the R8 specmap probe used Glob/Grep despite a Read/Edit/Write-only packet. Repeat the git/commit/full-panel/report clauses in the short pointer prompt: weak workers skim pointer indirection, and resumed threads may retain stale permissions.
facts.TEMPLATE-ROOT-CLOSE: After `TASK-DONE`, root mechanically compares actual changed files to the report, reads the diff, checks Decisions/Deviations, reruns decisive commands and red proofs, then accepts, sends exact `-c` repair notes, re-commissions or discards. The packet/template reduces review cost; it never replaces review.

p.HIST-OWNER-2026-08-26: Authored from the owner's 2026-08-26 rulings: use `claudez` and Opus/max alongside Sol/native workers because quotas are separate; never select Fable; consolidate the strategy in one ChatGPT-only document; keep the agent-instruction triplet byte-identical; replace per-atom full panels with exact gates and batch panels.
